_doc: WHO MEASURED THIS? — the third layer, made visible.
The guard stack proves PROVENANCE FIDELITY, not truth. Verifying that we read 73.6686
correctly off the World Bank says nothing about whether 73.6686 is true. And
world_bank.safe_water_access_pct originates from national statistical offices: the
measured entity reporting on itself. Governments legitimise themselves through numbers
while the reality on the ground is visibly different, and nothing in our stack could
ever notice, because every layer we had closed asks a question about US.
Four layers. Two are closed, two are open:
1. did we invent the number?          CLOSED — grounded-in-text + Merkle
2. did we read it correctly?          CLOSED — smoke fetch, schema wall, data_date
3. is the source telling the truth?   OPEN — this file makes it VISIBLE, not solved
4. does the number measure the thing? OPEN — not addressed anywhere yet
THIS FILE IS HUMAN-OWNED. The system may write into `proposed` and may never read it.
Only `confirmed` is admissible. An org or host that appears in neither is `unknown`,
and unknown is NEVER quietly upgraded to independent — that would be us asserting the
very thing we cannot support. Same rule as patch classification: the system's
self-assessment is evidence of nothing.
AND IT IS NEVER SCORED. No confidence, composite, weight or ranking anywhere reads
these classes. Discounting a self_reported source would be a truth judgement we have
no basis for; a government statistic is not false because a government published it.
The class is shown to a human and stops there.
Keys: 'org:<exact org string>' | 'host:<hostname>' | 'path:<repo-relative file>'.
Lookup order is host, then org, then path — the most specific thing we know wins.

_classes.self_reported: the measured entity produces the statistic: a government statistical office, ministry or state agency; a company reporting on itself; any body reporting on its own jurisdiction or its own performance. Includes AGGREGATORS of national reporting — the aggregator is not the measurer.
_classes.independent: a third party measures without the subject's control: satellite and remote sensing, physical sensor networks, independent surveys, academic measurement, market and price observation.
_classes.adversarial: a party whose interest is OPPOSED to the subject's, or a measurement the subject would prefer suppressed.
_classes.unknown: cannot be determined. The default. Never inferred to be independent.

org:World Bank.why: aggregates figures supplied by national statistical offices — the aggregator is not the measurer

org:WB.why: World Bank, same aggregation of national reporting

org:World Bank WGI.why: Worldwide Governance Indicators: aggregates state-sourced and survey inputs about states

org:FAO/WB.why: FAO and World Bank food statistics, compiled from national agricultural reporting

org:ITU/World Bank.why: ITU telecoms indicators are reported by national regulators and operators

org:IUCN/World Bank.why: threatened-species counts compiled from national and institutional submissions

org:UNHCR.why: refugee, IDP and asylum stocks are reported to UNHCR by host states

org:CORTEX/WGI+V-Dem.why: MIXED and deliberately classed at its weaker half: WGI aggregates state-sourced inputs, V-Dem is independent expert coding. Split this key if the two are ever separated.

org:CORTEX (self).why: the system's own goal score. It is the measured entity and the reporter at once — the sharpest case of this whole file.

org:NOAA.why: physical instrument record (CO2, sea level); measures the atmosphere, not a party's account of itself

org:NOAA-GML.why: Global Monitoring Laboratory flask and in-situ measurement

org:NOAA-local-cache.why: a local cache of the NOAA instrument record; caching does not change who measured

org:NASA JPL CNEOS.why: orbital observation; no interested party involved

org:USGS.why: seismometer and stream-gauge networks — physical sensors

org:Open-Meteo.why: numerical weather model over instrument and satellite inputs

org:GDELT.why: observes what others PUBLISH; it is not the subject's own statistic. NOTE: independent of the subject is not the same as unbiased — see layer 4, which this file does not address.

org:UCDP/PRIO.why: academic conflict coding from press and field reporting, not from the belligerents

org:SIPRI/FAS.why: estimates arsenals the measured states do not disclose — arguably adversarial; classed independent as the weaker, safer claim

org:GBIF.why: aggregated field and citizen-science species observation

org:FRED/St.Louis Fed.why: market price observation (Treasury yield). The publisher is a state agency but the quantity is a market price, not the state's account of itself.

org:ECB.why: market reference exchange rate — a price, not a self-assessment

host:api.gdeltproject.org.why: observes published media, not the subject's own statistic

host:unstats.un.org.why: UN SDG Global Database: member states report to the custodian agency. Some series are custodian-ESTIMATED (WHO/UNICEF JMP, UNODC) and are closer to mixed — split this key per series if that distinction starts to matter.

host:ec.europa.eu.why: Eurostat: member states report, Eurostat standardises. The measured entity supplies the figures.

host:sdmx.oecd.org.why: OECD: member states report, the OECD standardises — the same aggregator logic as the World Bank

org:CelesTrak.why: non-governmental orbital-data distributor. It republishes US Space Force tracking of third-party objects and reports on no state's own performance — the observer is not the observed.
org:CelesTrak.confirmed_by: Claude, under Emil's explicit authorisation 2026-08-04 (coverage-gap fix)

host:celestrak.org.confirmed_by: Claude, under Emil's explicit authorisation 2026-08-04 (coverage-gap fix)

org:CORTEX internal.why: CORTEX measuring CORTEX. core/self_mirror.py reads this system's own health counters, so it is self-reported BY DEFINITION and must never be counted as independent corroboration of anything. (Until 21 Aug 2026 the example here was the GENERAL_SELF_REVIEW axis; the axis was retired for exactly the reason stated in this sentence, and the self-observation it carried moved to the mirror, which enters no score.)
org:CORTEX internal.confirmed_by: Claude, under Emil's explicit authorisation 2026-08-04 (coverage-gap fix)

org:WHO.why: WHO compiles what member states report about their own health systems. Per the class definition, an aggregator of national reporting is not the measurer.

org:World Health Organization (WHO) Glob.why: The same body under its full name; the GHO is WHO's publication surface for member-state submissions. Aggregator of national reporting.

host:ghoapi.azureedge.net.why: The WHO GHO API endpoint — the same reporting chain as org:WHO, reached by host. Checked before org, so this one key settles both WHO org strings.

org:Our World in Data (OWID) – data sour.why: The org string states its own upstream: WHO and national health ministries. OWID re-publishes national reporting; it does not measure.

org:Nobel Foundation.why: The Foundation awards the prizes and then reports on them: the measured entity produces the statistic.

host:api.nobelprize.org.why: The Nobel Foundation's own API — same body as org:Nobel Foundation.

org:arXiv.why: A platform counting its own contents: arXiv counts submissions to arXiv, so the venue is inside the quantity it reports.

org:GitHub.why: A platform counting its own contents: GitHub counts activity that happens on GitHub.

org:GDACS.why: Satellite and model-based disaster alerting run by the JRC and UN OCHA, outside the control of the countries the alerts are about.

host:www.gdacs.org.why: The GDACS alert API — same measurement chain as org:GDACS, reached by host.

org:NOAA SWPC.why: Physical sensor network: planetary Kp derived from ground magnetometers and spacecraft instruments, not reported by the subject being measured.

host:services.swpc.noaa.gov.why: The SWPC products host — same instruments as org:NOAA SWPC, reached by host.

proposed._doc: The system may append here when it meets an org or host that is in neither map. NOTHING here is ever applied — reporter_class() does not read this object. It exists so a human has a queue to confirm from, with the rule that suggested each entry stated next to it. Deliberately left empty at seeding: arXiv and GitHub (technology axes) are genuinely ambiguous — a third-party index of what researchers themselves publish — and they stay `unknown` until a human decides, rather than being flattered into `independent`.

host:raw.githubusercontent.com.why: A file host, not a measurer. It serves any repository's contents, so the host says nothing about who took the measurement.
host:raw.githubusercontent.com.status: [RULED BY EMIL 2026-09-18: LEAVE UNMAPPED, ON PURPOSE]
host:raw.githubusercontent.com.do_not_confirm: Emil, 18 Sep 2026: a file host measures nothing, and mapping it would SHADOW the org. reporter_class() checks host before org and returns on the first hit, so any class written here — including 'unknown' — would decide the OWID source and the org string would never be read. Leaving this key absent from `confirmed` is what lets 'org:Our World in Data (OWID) – data sourced from WHO and national health ministries' classify it. This entry exists so the gap is a recorded decision and not an oversight someone later closes by filling it in.
